coding_note: Corps members serving as INEC ad hoc staff were injured by bomb blasts at a polling unit and a collation centre on National Assembly election day, so the stage is election duty and the harm is an explosion.
Six corps members who had sought refuge at a police station in their host area were killed by a mob during post-presidential-election violence.
Five serving corps members were abducted while carrying out a community development project in their host community; kidnappers demanded ransom and the outcome was not reported.

Three corps members working as election officials at a state assembly by-election were abducted by thugs and rescued minutes later, and a fourth was beaten; election duty is coded ppa and kidnapping is the most serious harm.

Armed men entered a lodge housing about 20 corps members at night, threatened them and took phones, laptops and allowances, so the stage is lodge during service and the harm is robbery. Day inferred from the weekday given in the report [A07].
A serving corps member was attacked with machetes at night while returning to her lodge near her place of primary assignment, losing a hand.
Two corps members were injured when a commuter bus collided with a car on the road near Abaji; no link to duty is stated.
Three corps members riding one motorcycle were hit by a truck; two died and one had minor injuries, with no link to duty stated.

Prospective corps member posted to Imo State, abducted at Rumuokoro after relatives dropped him off to travel to camp; ransom paid but he was never released or found, and suspects were charged over his death.
A corps member was shot dead by gunmen while conducting the Rivers re-run election, which is election duty coded ppa. Day inferred from the weekday given in the report [A07].
A female corps member was abducted by gunmen from a corps lodge in her host community and rescued by police after a gunfight.
A serving corps member was shot while sitting in his car in his host city at night and died on the way to hospital.

Corps members on election duty during the Rivers rerun election were abducted with election materials after explosions near the collation area and rescued by soldiers within hours. Election duty is coded ppa [A06]; an abduction at a second location the same day is recorded as a separate incident. Day inferred from the weekday given in the report [A07].

Corps members on election duty during the Rivers rerun election were abducted in a bus carrying election materials and rescued by soldiers. Election duty is coded ppa [A06]; recorded separately from the abduction in Akuku-Toru LGA the same day. Day inferred from the weekday given in the report [A07].

A female corps member travelling by commercial bus from Lagos to Abuja was abducted with two other women by gunmen who robbed passengers; ransom was to be demanded from families. Day inferred from the weekday given in the report [A07].
A serving corps member was attacked by hoodlums at her residence near her place of primary assignment and suffered a cut wound; nothing was reported stolen.
A commercial bus travelling from Jalingo to Lagos crashed on the Benue-Taraba highway, killing one corps member and injuring others including corps members; no duty link is stated.
A serving corps member days from the end of her service year was shot by suspected armed robbers trailing the car she was in within her host city, and died.
Serving corps members returning from the bank in their host community were robbed; one was taken away and released two days later. Kidnapping coded as the most serious harm; number robbed not stated.

Serving corps member posted to another state was shot and wounded by unknown gunmen while visiting his home village during the holiday period, travel with no link to duty. He survived; a non-corps relative was killed.

A serving corps member was lured by a driving instructor to a forest in her host area, sexually assaulted and strangled; killing outranks sexual violence. Day inferred from the weekday given in the report [A07].
Armed robbers attacked a corps members' lodge in the host community and severed one corps member's hand; physical assault ranks above robbery. Article gives only 'Sunday' in March 2018.
Newly posted serving corps member was shot dead by a naval officer during an altercation at a social gathering in the host community.

Serving corps members on a tricycle returning from final clearance ahead of their passing-out ceremony collided with a tipper truck; coded ppa because the journey preceded passing out and was a service-year clearance trip. Two died and two were injured. Duty-linked return journey to the posting coded ppa [A08].

Serving corps member was shot dead by a police officer at a checkpoint around 3 a.m. while leaving an outing with colleagues the day before her passing out; coded ppa as it occurred in the host community before the passing-out event.
A bus carrying 37 corps members from the orientation camp to their posting areas crashed on an expressway after over-speeding; 19 were injured and none died.

Corps member who had just finished orientation in another state was abducted by suspected cultists from his family home while visiting before resuming at his posting; no stated link to duty. No ransom demand had been reported and his fate was unknown at publication.

Serving corps member drowned when a canoe capsized at a dam during a recreational picnic marking the end of service in the host state; two others were rescued by fishermen. Day inferred from the weekday given in the report [A07].

Five corps members abducted on the Owerri-Port Harcourt Expressway while travelling to Rivers and Akwa Ibom; the report does not say whether the journey was to camp or to a posting, so stage and status are unknown.

Corps member serving with INEC died when the vehicle carrying INEC staff collided with a trailer while returning from a colleague's wedding, a social trip with no link to duty. Day inferred from the weekday given in the report [A07].
A vehicle conveying 17 corps members with NYSC and state officials to their primary assignment postings crashed; 10 were seriously and 7 slightly injured, no deaths.

Serving corps member was fatally stabbed by a youth during an altercation at a politician's residence during a political gathering in the host community. Perpetrators described as political thugs/local youths, coded unknown.
Corps member abducted by Boko Haram in January 2019 and released in June 2019; activity at the time of abduction not reported.

A serving corps member on general election duty was abducted and later released; election duty is coded as ppa. A separate attack on corps members at a collation centre in Idemili North on 2019-02-24, with injuries, appears in the same report and is not a candidate in this batch.

Corps members serving as INEC ad hoc staff abducted during the presidential and National Assembly elections in their state of service; incidents in Uruan and Ikono LGAs reported together, so LGA is left blank; some released after security intervention.
Gunmen suspected to be cultists invaded the residence of three corps members attached to a nearby school and opened fire, killing two and wounding one.
Six prospective corps members travelling by commercial vehicle to the orientation camp were robbed of phones and valuables by armed robbers around 1 a.m.; no injuries reported.

Four serving corps members travelling by commercial bus from Lagos to Port Harcourt were abducted and later rescued by police in a forest operation; no stated link to duty. Article says only that the abduction was 'last week'.

A bus conveying corps members from the orientation camp to their posting local government at the end of orientation collided head-on with a minibus; one died and others were injured. Injured count of 19 included a local government inspector, so corps member total is approximate. Day inferred from the weekday given in the report [A07].
Corps member serving with a television station was fatally shot while covering a clash between police and protesters as part of his work; who fired the shot was disputed.
Corps members travelling by bus to attend a mass wedding organised by a corps religious fellowship crashed; a private trip with no stated link to duty.

Serving corps member attached to a local government secretariat was abducted from her residence around 4:30 a.m. and freed the same night. Kidnappers demanded N5m; security sources said N600,000 was paid.

Eight corps members travelling at night from an orientation camp in another state toward Port Harcourt were injured in a crash on a bypass; coded travel_to_ppa as a journey leaving camp at end of orientation. No deaths.
Serving corps member abducted on her way to a community development service meeting at Ilamija; ransom demanded but not paid; rescued by police.
A corps member on primary assignment in Uyo was gang-raped by two men at their house where she had gone to charge her phone; incident date not stated, suspects' arrest reported 9 June 2020.

A serving corps member was among passengers of a commercial bus returning from Yuletide celebrations who were shot by a mobile police officer after a dispute with the driver; coded physical assault because police stated victims were responding to treatment. Day inferred from the weekday given in the report [A07].
A serving corps member was shot dead by armed robbers while closing his recharge card shop at night in his host community; recharge cards and cash were taken.
A corps member serving in the FCT was abducted with eight other passengers when gunmen in military-style uniforms stopped a commuter bus travelling to Lokoja; no duty link for the journey was stated.
Four prospective corps members abducted on the Funtua-Gusau road on their way to the Gusau orientation camp; rescued by police with help from repentant bandits.
A serving corps member attached to a school in Sagamu was among two captives rescued when police chased a kidnappers' vehicle and killed one suspect; where and when she was seized is not stated.
A serving corps member posted to Obio/Akpor was sexually assaulted after being invited to a residence in her host community for a birthday celebration; two private individuals were arrested.

A corps member travelling north with 16 others on the day they left the Osun orientation camp was shot dead by armed robbers firing sporadically on the highway; journey leaving camp at end of orientation.
Five prospective corps members died in a road crash on the Abaji/Kwali expressway while travelling from the south to the Katsina orientation camp.

Two prospective corps members travelling from Benue to the Kebbi and Sokoto camps abducted by bandits on the Tsafe-Gusau road; released with four other passengers after ransom demands. May be linked to the abduction reported for 20 October in the same LGA, but no report connects them.
Prospective corps member on the way to the Kebbi orientation camp abducted with other passengers in Tsafe LGA; escaped after four days and went on to camp.

Five corps members died when their bus collided with a tractor as they travelled home to Yobe after completing the 21-day orientation course in Taraba; journey leaving camp at end of orientation. The Oyo crash in the same article involved labourers only.

A serving corps member went missing with her infant after a CDS activity and was later found dead; police said she was lured to a private residence and murdered by a romantic rival and accomplices, so coded as killing rather than kidnapping for ransom.
A corps member serving in Abuja, travelling toward Kaduna in a commercial vehicle, was killed by a stray bullet during a crossfire between security forces and bandits crossing the highway.
Two corps members were among those who drowned when a boat capsized in bad weather on a waterway in Southern Ijaw; purpose of the journey is not stated.
Armed men forced entry into a corps members' lodge at night and took phones, laptops and cash; coded robbery because the NYSC state coordinator denied the reported rapes.
A corps member was among five killed when a speeding bus crashed into a ditch in heavy rain on the Abuja-Lokoja road; purpose of travel and service status not stated.
Two serving female corps members were abducted in their host community while buying medicine at a chemist; a N25 million ransom was demanded.
A corps member among six people abducted on the Obollo Afor-Nkalagu road after a community security meeting; the report does not link the journey to service duties or give the outcome.
Fifteen corps members travelling to Lagos at the end of the orientation course in Imo State were intercepted at Ihiala; rescued unhurt by police the same day [A05].
Seven corps members abducted while travelling to Rivers State after the orientation course in Ondo State; released about a week later at Rumuji; one family reported paying ransom [A05].

Two female corps members drowned when the bus taking them from Onitsha to Calabar for their primary assignment plunged into a river in Enugu State; coded travel to PPA as the journey was to the posting.

Eight prospective corps members travelling by state transport bus from Uyo to the Sokoto camp abducted on the Funtua-Gusau road; ransom demanded; all freed by August 2024, the last after a year in captivity; NYSC states no ransom was paid.

A serving female corps member was stabbed and killed by attackers on a motorcycle attempting to snatch her phone while she was jogging early in the morning near her lodge area. Day inferred from the weekday given in the report [A07].

Two corps members abducted by bandits at Yargoje while travelling from Edo to Katsina; rescued on 2 November 2023. The abduction date is not reported, so the month of rescue is used, and the reports do not link the journey to service duties.

A female corps member was killed by robbers on the Naka-Makurdi road while trying to protect her laptop; date given only as earlier in 2024, before the 6 February arrests, and purpose of travel not stated.

A corps member serving in Katsina died in a road crash while travelling from Kaduna back to his posting for monthly biometric clearance, a duty-linked journey; NYSC denied rumours of banditry. Duty-linked return journey to the posting coded ppa [A08].

A corps member serving elsewhere in the state was shot dead when police fired shots while dispersing a crowd at a nightclub during a family graduation celebration in another town; shooting death by police coded as killing.

Corps members returning from the orientation camp abducted on the Ifon-Owo road; the driver and a female passenger were killed; ransom paid and the captives abandoned under police pressure [A05, C05].

A female corps member was beaten, slapped and had her uniform torn by teachers when she went to her place of primary assignment to collect her clearance letter. Perpetrators were staff at the posting school, which does not fit the listed perpetrator categories. Day inferred from the weekday given in the report [A07].

A corps member serving in Abuja was killed at the residence of a male acquaintance she visited in a neighbouring state; there was no link to duty. The perpetrator was an individual later convicted, which does not fit the listed group categories.
Prospective corps members among about 35 passengers abducted from three buses on the Enugu-Nsukka road; one was travelling to NYSC service in Kogi State; number of corps members not stated.
A commercial bus carrying prospective corps members from Enugu to the orientation camp crashed into a tipper truck; this is a road crash during travel to camp.

A serving corps member was struck on the head by motorcycle snatchers while riding home in the evening and died the next night; a robbery that killed is coded as killing. The stage is unknown because the article places his posting outside the area where he lived.

Operatives of a state government security outfit pursuing suspected cultists assaulted a female corps member and stripped her; the article does not state her location or activity. Day inferred from the weekday given in the report [A07].

A corps member serving in another state was abducted with a student when gunmen broke into a family home where she was preparing for her wedding; this is personal travel with no link to duty. Day inferred from the weekday given in the report [A07].
Prospective corps member abducted on the Kogi axis on the way to the Taraba orientation camp; N30 million demanded; still held as last reported on 30 January 2026.

A serving female corps member died of reported complications after a pregnancy termination, and an NYSC official was arrested over the death; this is coded as other external harm pending investigation. Inclusion is uncertain because the reports do not say who carried out the procedure. Day inferred from the weekday given in the report [A07].

A corps member posted in the same city was killed by gunmen in a reprisal attack on a community while operating a motorcycle, shortly before passing out; he was in his host community during the service year. Day inferred from the weekday given in the report [A07].

A corps member serving in another state was beaten to death by community vigilantes who wrongly accused him of motorcycle theft while he was in his home state. Day inferred from the weekday given in the report [A07].

A serving corps member, retained at his place of primary assignment, was shot dead by soldiers inside his room at his residence; shooting by security forces is coded as killing. Day inferred from the weekday given in the report [A07].
Four serving corps members on a commercial bus between two towns in their state of service died when it collided with a military truck and caught fire; no link to duty was stated.
Corps members travelling in two commercial buses to Abuja after the orientation course in Bayelsa State abducted on the Itobe-Onicha-Igo axis; all rescued by security forces within a week [A05, C02].

Prospective corps members travelling from Ibadan to orientation camps in Akwa Ibom and Abia abducted from two buses on the Owerri-Onitsha road at Umunoha; 10 victims rescued the same day; the rest still held as last reported [C03, C04].
